subject: English Core
title: The Rattrap — Prose Chapter 4 - Part 2 DPP

questions.question: Which detail best highlights the harsh working conditions in the forge?
options: The use of wooden shoes
The glow of light through the panes
The men dripping with perspiration despite minimal clothing
The noise of the waterfall outside
questions.explanation: The men dripping with perspiration despite minimal clothing

questions.question: The author’s description of the forge emphasises:
options: Stillness and solemnity
A chaotic mix of sounds and activity
The luxury of the iron mill
The warmth and silence of the workplace

questions.question: Why did the blacksmiths not pay attention to the tramp?
options: They were afraid of him
They mistook him for the ironmaster
Vagabonds often came to the forge for warmth
They were instructed not to speak to strangers
questions.explanation: Vagabonds often came to the forge for warmth

questions.question: The tramp decided not to reveal his real identity to the ironmaster because:
options: He enjoyed deceiving people
He thought it might earn him some money
He wanted to avenge himself on the ironmaster
He planned to steal from the forge
questions.explanation: He thought it might earn him some money

questions.question: The tramp’s reluctance to visit the manor house is described as:
options: Embarrassment due to his clothes
Fear of being exposed and caught
Desire to return to his regiment
Annoyance with the blacksmiths
questions.explanation: Fear of being exposed and caught

questions.question: Which quality of Edla Willmansson ultimately persuaded the tramp?
options: Her stern authority
Her gentle compassion and reassurance
Her father’s wealth
Her insistence on military discipline

questions.question: Edla’s thought, “Either he has stolen something or else he has escaped from jail,” reveals her:
options: Trusting innocence
Sharp intuition despite compassion
Cold suspicion
Lack of judgment

questions.question: The ironmaster’s disappointment the next morning arose from:
options: His daughter’s compassion
The tramp’s refusal to leave
The recognition that he had mistaken a stranger for his comrade
The failure of the forge work

questions.question: Which statement best captures the thematic relevance of this episode?
options: Human dignity is more important than material wealth
Loneliness often leads people to seek false companionship

questions.question: The tramp’s words, “At worst I can put on my rags again and go away,” signify:
options: His indifference towards the ironmaster’s anger
His readiness to leave without confrontation
His acceptance of the temporary nature of borrowed respectability
His arrogance against the wealthy | | Android App iOS App PW Website
questions.explanation: His acceptance of the temporary nature of borrowed respectability
